researchStatement: My published work is all **computer vision**, applied across four different problems: detecting synthetic images, screening for eye disease, classifying rice leaf disease, and fusing evidence for medical AI. Eighteen months at **Othello** added the production side: tracking, pose estimation and activity recognition running on live video, including a first hands-on look at **IoT edge devices** feeding those pipelines.

The forensic invariant paper looks for cues that survive a change of image generator rather than artefacts a classifier memorises. BD Eye-Doc pairs a vision classifier with a conversational interface for places without a specialist. The rice leaf study compares CNNs, ensembles and **Vision Transformers** under real compute limits. RGEF uses **evidential reliability gating** so a medical AI model can abstain instead of guess.

What I want to work on next is where **AI meets hardware directly**: robotics, automation and embedded systems, rather than vision applied to static images alone. That means perception under real actuation and control constraints, not just classification accuracy, and I am looking for a research-based Master's in robotics, automation or embedded AI where I can make that shift properly.

researchAreas.title: Edge AI
researchAreas.desc: Perception that has to run on the device rather than in a data centre — and the widening gap between how fast models are advancing and how slowly the hardware underneath them is. At Othello, getting models onto **IoT edge devices** feeding real-time vision pipelines was the hard part, and parallel inference optimisation cut processing latency by **~70%** only by trading complexity against a fixed budget. I want to study how far those choices carry under the tighter latency and power constraints of embedded hardware.

researchAreas.title: Robotics & Automation
researchAreas.desc: AI that couples directly to hardware, sensors and real-time control rather than to images alone. My Research Assistant work was empirical Human–Robot Interaction; the ADAS lane and vehicle detection project is perception for a system that has to act; and RGEF's reliability gating is the closest I have come to a model deciding when not to act at all.

researchAreas.title: Perception
researchAreas.desc: Making sense of a scene reliably enough to act on it, and knowing when that reading cannot be trusted. My four papers come at this from different angles: detecting synthetic imagery through physics-informed invariants, eye disease screening for low-resource clinics, CNNs against Vision Transformers under real compute limits, and evidential gating so a model can abstain instead of guess.

researchAreas.title: Tracking, activity recognition & pose estimation
researchAreas.desc: Multi-object tracking, human activity recognition and pose estimation on live video. Built and shipped in production at Othello (ByteTrack, MoveNet, MMAction2), and the same perceptual problem underlies the rice leaf and BD Eye-Doc classification studies.

publications.title: Forensic Invariant Learning for Synthetic Image Detection: Bridging Benford's Law and Topological Analysis with Machine Learning Ensembles
publications.authors: **Md Abu Sayeb Rayhan**, Ajoy Shutradhar, Hustagna Hiya
publications.venue: IEEE International Conference on Quantum Photonics, Artificial Intelligence and Networking (QPAIN) 2026
publications.note: Detecting AI-generated imagery through **physics-informed invariants** rather than learned artefacts. It combines Benford's Law digit statistics with topological features across a six-model ensemble, targeting cues that survive a change of generator. That is the failure mode most detectors share.

bullets: Built **multi-object tracking** (ByteTrack), **pose estimation** (MoveNet) and **human activity recognition** (MMAction2) pipelines for automated behaviour analysis on live retail video.
Designed a spatial clustering pipeline applying **OPTICS** to pose-estimation output for group-dynamics modelling; parallel inference optimisation reduced processing latency by **~70%**.
Developed a video **event-segmentation** system on a fine-tuned YOLO detector at **90%+ accuracy**, automating highlight extraction and cutting production cost by **50%**.
Implemented a **retrieval-augmented generation** system (LangChain, Pinecone, GPT-4) for context-aware document querying, deployed on **Microsoft Azure**.
Integrated IoT edge devices feeding real-time computer vision pipelines for automated data acquisition.
Developed a multilingual (Bangla/English) **NLP and OCR** retrieval pipeline spanning PDF, Word, Excel and image formats, combining optical character recognition with **dense embeddings**.
Shipped as a desktop application built with PyQt and ChromaDB.
**Led a three-person team** across the full product lifecycle, from design through deployment.
Conducted empirical studies in **Human–Robot Interaction** and **Optical Character Recognition**, covering dataset design, experimental protocol and quantitative analysis.
Prepared and validated results subsequently incorporated into **peer-reviewed conference publications**.

projects.title: eGP AutoPilot
projects.desc: My **first startup product**: a bilingual (English/Bengali) desktop application that automates tender submission on the **Bangladesh e-Government Procurement portal**. It drives the portal through Playwright — login, form filling, encryption and signing, document mapping and a verification pass — and keeps going through crashes, network drops and half-finished runs.
projects.impact: First startup product · v2.2.0, shipping on macOS and Windows
projects.role: Founder · solo design, build and release
projects.problem: Preparing a tender on the national e-GP portal is long, repetitive and unforgiving: one unfilled form or unmapped document can invalidate a bid, and the work has to be redone from the start if the connection drops.
details: Drives the portal end to end with **Playwright** — login, Tenderer Info, Activities, Personnel and Priced BOQ forms, then click-sign, encrypt and save.
Resumes exactly where it stopped. Per-account state is written to disk, so a crash or a two-minute network drop does not cost the whole run.
Every failing row gets five attempts, then five more in a deferred pass; anything still failing is **reported rather than silently skipped**.
Maps uploaded files to the portal's document categories by fuzzy filename match — trade licence, TIN, VAT, liquid assets.
Runs from a phone: a mobile dashboard over a REST API with QR-code pairing, and no credentials sent over the wire.
Firebase-backed accounts, subscriptions and **bKash** billing, with an admin panel for users, plans, devices and payments.
Packaged for macOS and Windows, behind 273 offline tests that never touch the production database.
projects.researchNote: Reliability engineering against a system I do not control. Every step retries, defers and resumes from saved state, because the portal, the network and the user's machine each fail in a different way — the same instinct behind wanting a model to abstain rather than guess.

projects.title: Why I Saved This — browser memory
projects.desc: A browser extension that remembers **why** you saved something, not just where. It keeps the page, the passage you highlighted and your own note together, then brings you back to the exact spot months later with the note in the margin beside it.
details: Save a page, a highlighted passage, a link or an image — from the toolbar, the context menu, or one shortcut that works out which you meant.
Search runs on **your own notes and highlights first**, ranking them above titles and URLs.
Re-anchors to the saved passage even when the page has changed since, scrolls to it, and lights up every highlight from that page with its note alongside.
Entirely local: **no account, no server, no sync, no analytics, no network requests**. Installing asks for no site access at all.
Licence keys are signed tokens verified on the device, because there is no server to check them against.
TypeScript and React on WXT, Dexie over IndexedDB, MiniSearch for retrieval, with unit tests in Vitest and end-to-end tests in Playwright.

projects.title: Universal NFT Generation Platform
projects.desc: Generalised a sports-specific video system into a platform handling **user-generated footage** across festivals, concerts and other domains. Fine-tuned **action detection** models and built the pipeline for automated clip creation.
projects.impact: Extended a single-domain system to open-domain video
projects.problem: A video pipeline tuned for one controlled sport had to keep working on user-generated footage from festivals, concerts and other domains it was never built for.
projects.experiment: Action-detection models fine-tuned on the original sports setting were run against unconstrained user video, and the clip-creation pipeline rebuilt around what survived the change of domain.
projects.researchNote: Domain generalisation in practice: an action-recognition pipeline tuned for one controlled setting, then forced to hold up on unconstrained user video.

projects.title: Real-Time In-Store Behaviour Analytics
projects.desc: Real-time system detecting customer groupings and product interest from in-store camera feeds using pose estimation and density-based spatial clustering. Parallelised inference brought latency down sharply.
projects.problem: Reading how customers group and where their interest falls, from ordinary in-store camera feeds, fast enough for the answer to still be useful.
projects.experiment: Pose estimation feeding density-based spatial clustering was run on live store cameras; parallelising inference brought processing latency down by about 70%.
projects.researchNote: Pose estimation coupled with density-based clustering under a hard latency budget: evidence for perception under real deployment constraints.

projects.title: Sports NFT Generation System
projects.desc: Trained a custom object detection model and built a real-time video processing pipeline that identifies key moments in sports footage and generates clips without human intervention.
projects.problem: Finding the moments worth keeping in raw sports footage without a person having to watch the whole match.
details: Detects players, the ball and the basket with **YOLOv8**, then tracks them across frames with DeepSORT or ByteTrack.
Keeps ball tracking smooth through brief occlusion using trajectory interpolation and **Kalman filtering**.
Recognises key actions and classifies highlight-worthy events from motion and positional data.
Compiles the final reel automatically: auto zoom on the action, slow-motion replay, transitions and metadata overlay.
Derives per-player statistics — shots, passes and time on court.
projects.experiment: A custom detector was trained and run over full-length game video, reaching 90% detection accuracy and producing highlight clips with no human in the loop — cutting production cost by half.
projects.researchNote: Multi-object tracking and temporal event segmentation on unconstrained broadcast video, where occlusion and camera motion are the hard cases.

projects.title: Context Searcher
projects.desc: RAG-based desktop application for keyword and semantic search across PDF, DOCX, XLSX, TXT and images in Bengali and English, combining OCR with dense embeddings.
projects.problem: Searching a mixed pile of office documents and scanned images by meaning rather than exact keyword, in a low-resource language where that is much harder.
projects.experiment: OCR combined with dense embeddings was exercised across PDF, DOCX, XLSX, TXT and image files in both Bengali and English, and shipped as a desktop application.
projects.researchNote: Multimodal retrieval across text and images in a low-resource language (Bangla), combining OCR with dense embeddings.

projects.title: Text-to-Image Generation using Diffusion Models
projects.desc: Bachelor's thesis. Fine-tuned **Stable Diffusion** with a U-Net backbone on a purpose-built dataset of Bangladeshi landmarks, examining prompt engineering and **conditioning mechanisms** as levers on generative fidelity, with OpenCV post-processing to reduce artefacts.
projects.problem: Whether a general text-to-image model can be fine-tuned to render a specific, under-represented subject faithfully — in this case Bangladeshi landmarks.
projects.experiment: Stable Diffusion with a U-Net backbone was fine-tuned on a purpose-built dataset of those landmarks, varying prompts and conditioning to see how each moved generative fidelity, with OpenCV post-processing to reduce artefacts.
projects.researchNote: The origin of the generative-model thread in my research: diffusion-model fine-tuning and conditioning, which the forensic invariant learning paper later turned around into a detection problem.

projects.title: ILLUSION — Virtual Object Control by Hand Gesture
projects.desc: Real-time **hand tracking** and gesture control: webcam frames are processed to detect hand landmarks and fingertips, and pinch/grab gestures are mapped to a virtual object that can be dragged in real time.
projects.impact: Runs live on a webcam feed
projects.problem: Driving an on-screen object with nothing but a webcam and your hands, at a speed that still feels like direct manipulation.
details: Processes the webcam feed frame by frame.
Detects and tracks **hand landmarks and fingertips**.
Maps finger position and pinch/grab gestures to a virtual object so it can be dragged in real time.
projects.experiment: Hand landmarks and fingertips were detected frame by frame on a live webcam feed and pinch/grab gestures mapped to a virtual object, which can be dragged in real time.
projects.researchNote: Real-time human-machine interaction from vision alone, closely related to the Human–Robot Interaction studies I ran as a Research Assistant.

projects.title: ADAS Lane & Vehicle Detection
projects.desc: Real-time lane boundary and vehicle detection for driver-assistance systems, combining a **YOLOv5** detector fine-tuned on a custom dataset with classical computer vision for lane geometry.
projects.problem: Detecting lane boundaries and surrounding vehicles in road footage reliably enough to sit underneath lane-keeping and collision-warning behaviour.
details: Detects vehicles in road footage with a **YOLOv5** model fine-tuned on a custom dataset.
Detects lane boundaries and overlays them on the video stream.
Outputs a single annotated video combining both — the building blocks of lane-keeping and collision-warning systems.
Split across three notebooks: dataset preparation, YOLOv5 training/inference, and the full end-to-end pipeline.
projects.experiment: A YOLOv5 detector fine-tuned on a custom dataset was combined with classical lane-geometry vision and run end-to-end over road video, producing a single annotated stream — the demo output is in stacked.mp4.
projects.researchNote: Perception for a system that has to act: the closest existing work to my robotics and embedded AI direction.

projects.title: RAG Customer Support Chatbot
projects.desc: End-to-end retrieval-augmented chatbot that retrieves relevant context from a vector index and generates grounded answers. Built and deployed solo on Azure.
details: Documents are loaded, chunked and embedded, then stored in a **Pinecone** vector index.
At query time the most relevant chunks are retrieved by similarity search and passed to the LLM as context.
**LangChain** orchestrates retrieval and generation so the answer stays grounded in the retrieved content.
Served through a Flask web interface and deployed on **Microsoft Azure**.

projects.title: Paper Summarizer Chatbot
projects.desc: LLM-powered chatbot that reads research papers and generates concise summaries, then answers grounded follow-up questions about the paper.
details: Takes a research paper as a PDF, then extracts and processes its content.
Generates a **structured summary** — problem, method, results.
Exposes a chat interface for follow-up questions about the same paper.

futureDirections.q: Models are advancing far faster than the hardware meant to run them. What gives first?
futureDirections.a: AI moves quickly; the silicon it has to run on does not, and that gap is getting wider rather than narrower. At **Othello** it was the daily problem — getting the models onto **edge devices** at all was a real challenge, and parallel inference optimisation only bought its **~70%** latency reduction by trading model complexity against a fixed processing budget. Retail video is a generous budget next to a robot. I want to study where that trade-off breaks as the gap widens, and whether the architectural choices that worked there still apply under the far tighter latency and power constraints of an embedded platform.

futureDirections.q: Can a model's own uncertainty drive a robot's actions, not just flag them?
futureDirections.a: RGEF stops at weighting and abstaining on a single decision. The useful extension is whether that same evidential state can feed a control loop directly: slowing a system down, triggering a sensor check, or handing off to a human, in real time rather than as an offline diagnostic. That is what turns reliability estimation into a control problem.

futureDirections.q: What perceptual structure survives when the sensor or hardware changes?
futureDirections.a: The forensic invariant work looked for cues that persist across different image generators. The same question applies to a robot or embedded system moving between cameras, lighting conditions and constrained onboard compute. I want to know how far that invariant-seeking approach carries over from detecting synthetic images to holding perception steady on real hardware in the field.

futureDirections.q: Does activity recognition survive the move from a fixed camera to one that moves?
futureDirections.a: Everything I have built for tracking, activity recognition and pose estimation assumed a camera that stays put: **ByteTrack**, **MoveNet** and **MMAction2** running on live retail video, with OPTICS clustering on top of the pose output. A robot carries its own camera, so ego-motion, a shifting viewpoint and self-occlusion all arrive at once. I want to know how much of that pipeline transfers and which parts have to be rebuilt rather than retuned. The closest thing I have to a first answer is the Universal NFT work, where models tuned on one controlled setting had to hold up on unconstrained user video.
